key_insight: Aegis protects federated medical training by adding a client-generated masking gradient that overwhelms model inversion attacks without changing patient data or the FL protocol.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals train shared diagnostic models with less risk of patient image leakage while preserving model utility.
method: Clients synthesize local, task-relevant data to create a masking gradient.
The masking update is superimposed on the real gradient, effectively increasing the attacker's required batch size beyond recovery limits.
The paper also provides convergence guarantees under standard convex assumptions.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and three MedMNIST medical imaging tasks (chest X-ray, abdominal CT, colon pathology) and reportedly neutralized three state-of-the-art model inversion attacks with modest overhead.
watch_item: The approach depends on locally synthesized masking data and theoretical guarantees under convex assumptions, so real-world performance may vary across architectures, tasks, and deployment settings.
paper_title: Aegis: Generative Gradient Masking for Privacy-Preserving Medical Federated Learning
